reason: Concrete Wry IPC/store boundary; payload-free ID selection and retention are tested in RequestLogStore, but a headless mock cannot supply this desktop AppHandle.
Native window visibility calls require the real window manager; the may_hide decision and stale frontend callbacks are tested independently.

Native recording command wiring requires Wry, capture and application stores. The delegated journal preparation, file-backed duration, recovery ownership, stale-session cancellation, retry replacement and waveform IPC are exercised without hardware.

Re-reviewed 2026-10-01: the existing unreachable serialization-error closure moved into the shared atomic snapshot writer. HistoryData contains only serializable plain fields. Retry and superseded-row success/failure, title preservation, correction protection, disk-write rollback and post-commit cleanup failure are exercised in storage tests; no transition or persistence behavior is waived.

Re-reviewed and approved 2026-09-30: concrete Wry command dispatch into the platform-owned input wrapper needs a desktop AppHandle. Actual portal request sequencing, paste chords, cleanup and restored grants are tested without touching user input.

Concrete desktop IPC wrappers invoke the OS compositor on a blocking worker. Parser, privacy and program-picker behavior have deterministic tests; compositor availability is a native acceptance check.
Wry settings-store and actual foreground-process lookup glue. Profile resolution, explicit system override, invalid-value inheritance and serialization are unit-tested in this module.

Re-reviewed and explicitly approved 2026-10-01: only real recording/permission callback wiring and its stale-session exits require the live capture/desktop event loop. Pipeline lease tests cover ownership decisions; superseded History and scoped-log success, cancellation, repeat, deletion and disk-failure behavior are tested with mock and real Wry handles. No History/clipboard helper logic is exempted. Removed the old autostart-registration exception because isolated full-app startup now executes that line.
Window event emission and the long-lived native waveform loop require the desktop event loop; notification ownership, waveform smoothing and listener teardown are independently tested.

Re-reviewed and approved 2026-09-30: concrete Wry live-output dispatch selects a blocking Linux/Windows worker or the macOS main thread. Streaming and cancellation semantics are tested without an OS clipboard; actual key delivery remains native acceptance. No Wayland live partial injection is enabled.

Successful managed-auth refresh needs the native credential store and a Supabase session; the post-refresh cancellation-under-lock defense is race-only. Missing-session failure cleanup, token-error classification and STT retry behavior are tested.

Two cancellation guards inside hashing/between worker completion and upload are race-only. Boundary cancellation, cancellation during sample read, checkpoint resume and complete chunk assembly are tested. Listed function-only exceptions are duplicate LLVM generic instances, not source-body waivers.

LLVM emits uncalled generic copies for early-return/cancelled/native callers. These source functions and every changed line execute in successful routing, rewrite, unavailable-provider and cancellation tests; only duplicate function records may be waived.

Re-reviewed and explicitly approved 2026-10-01: native final-output dispatch into the app-owned clipboard/portal/main-thread wrapper, including forwarding its request ID, requires desktop permission/input acceptance. Output-intent, portal sequencing and keyboard-order tests cover the owned behavior; mock and real Wry tests verify that late output warnings never modify a newer request. The scoped warning helper itself is fully covered and not exempted.
Native best-effort cost event adapter receives no audio for OCR-only usage; this concrete AppHandle call requires desktop acceptance.

Concrete Wry history/log/cost finalization adapters now forward duration rather than decoding a whole recording. Duration extraction, activity metadata and log finalization semantics are independently tested.
Read a non-secret paste setting from the concrete Wry store. Parser/default/inheritance/persistence tests cover the delegated value semantics.
Window-manager hide callback; tested may_hide predicate prevents active recording from disappearing.

Re-reviewed and approved 2026-09-30: native shortcut callback starts asynchronous app-owned output, requiring Wry/history stores. Release debounce, profile resolution, portal reuse and keyboard chords are deterministically tested.

Re-reviewed and approved 2026-09-30: native retry forwards the profile shortcut into awaited app-owned output; actual Wry input cannot run headlessly. Retry ownership, replacement, profile resolution and portal lifecycle have deterministic tests.

Concrete AppHandle cost-emission adapter converting optional WAV metadata to duration. Memory/file duration metadata is exercised by recording tests; actual native cost emission remains a desktop acceptance check.

Actual arboard clipboard read/OS wait cannot run safely in ordinary tests without touching the user's clipboard. Deterministic barrier tests cover immediate confirmation, busy/stale retries and fail-closed exhaustion; duplicate generic instance exception requires a covered source definition.

Re-reviewed and approved 2026-09-30: real Wry state capture, worker/main-thread dispatch, OS clipboard and native keyboard calls cannot safely execute in headless tests. Actual pipeline leases, portal permission/delivery lifecycle, chord cleanup, fallback policy and clipboard barriers are tested. No exception covers the lease comparison or controller protocol bodies.

Approved 2026-09-30: native media dispatch requires Wry and real keyboard input. The tested portal controller never prompts for optional media, reuses an approved grant and releases keys after failure; recording-side native invocation remains manual acceptance.

Approved 2026-09-30: OS keyring entry construction and serialized store access cannot safely use the real account keyring in headless tests. Isolated keyring credential tests cover rotation, failed-write preservation, idempotent removal and sanitized errors; renderer access to this grant is rejected.

Approved 2026-09-30: platform detection and real Enigo construction interact with native permission/input services. The permission-prompt latch, configured paste chords and cleanup are tested without asking the OS for user input approval.
Approved 2026-09-30: only the target-gated module declaration has no executable coverage records. The declared portal implementation is measured and tested; this is not a module-body exclusion.

Re-reviewed 2026-10-01: removed covered clipboard preparation/portal-denial exceptions after isolated Xvfb regression tests verified rejection without reading stale text, sentinel restoration after delivery failure and successful selection capture. Retained only the previously approved native keyboard and real Wry portal/main-thread dispatch boundaries; no new preparation or denial logic is waived. Actual desktop focus/grant restoration remains native acceptance. Re-reviewed 2026-10-02: added an explicit Result<(), String> return type to the covered preparation closure for Windows compilation; exception locations and behavior are unchanged.

Approved 2026-09-30: Wry/global-controller dispatch, session-bus and OS keyring workers are native boundaries. Four defensive lines handle failure subscribing to the compositor Closed signal and abort/close instead of using an unobservable grant. Request sequencing, registry identity, denial, restoration, revocation signal, keyboard-only persistence, rotation and all chord failure cleanup run against an isolated real D-Bus. Instantiation entries waive only duplicate LLVM records whose source and function execute in those tests.

Actual GNOME/KWin/X11/Sway/Hyprland IPC and uncommon OS temp-file/process errors require their desktop or fault injection. Backend selection, all response parsers, title opt-in/self filtering, helper failures, bounded output and malformed UTF-8 are covered. The ignored KWin smoke is intentionally not claimed as run.
Unused shortcut parameter in the Linux no-UIA fallback; actual Windows UIA requires Windows-native acceptance. Clipboard/key fallback logic has deterministic tests.

No executable Linux body: this selector re-exports the tested Linux implementation. Changed Windows Result wrapper and unsupported-platform fallback require their native target. Only these exact changed declarations may lack Linux coverage records.
